title: Paul's Defense Before King Agrippa

questions.question: Paul was permitted to speak before Agrippa. He stretched out his hand and said he considered himself fortunate to make his defense before Agrippa especially because Agrippa was familiar with what?
options: All the customs and controversies of the Jews
The writings of the prophets and the Law of Moses
The teachings of the Pharisees among whom Paul was raised
The political situation in Rome and the emperor's religious policies
questions.correctAnswer: All the customs and controversies of the Jews
questions.explanation: Acts 26:3 (ESV): "especially because you are familiar with all the customs and controversies of the Jews. Therefore I beg you to listen to me patiently."

questions.question: Paul said the reason he was on trial was for the hope of the promise made by God to the fathers. He said "the twelve tribes" earnestly hoped to attain this promise night and day. What was this hope?
options: The resurrection from the dead
The coming of the Messiah to reign in Jerusalem
The restoration of the kingdom to Israel
The outpouring of the Holy Spirit upon all flesh
questions.explanation: Acts 26:6-8 (ESV): "And now I stand here on trial because of my hope in the promise made by God to our fathers... Why is it thought incredible by any of you that God raises the dead?"

questions.question: Paul described his former zeal against Christians in Jerusalem. What had he obtained authority to do against the saints?
options: To shut them up in prison; he also cast his vote against them when they were put to death
To drag them from synagogues and flog them publicly
To expel them from Judea by order of the high priest
To confiscate their property and scatter their families
questions.correctAnswer: To shut them up in prison; he also cast his vote against them when they were put to death
questions.explanation: Acts 26:10 (ESV): "And I did so in Jerusalem. I not only locked up many of the saints in prison after receiving authority from the chief priests, but when they were put to death I cast my vote against them."

questions.question: Paul said he persecuted the saints "in a raging fury" so much that he even did what when pursuing them to foreign cities?
options: Persecuted them even to foreign cities
Organized armed bands to hunt them in Persia and Arabia
Wrote letters to every synagogue across the Roman Empire
Convinced the Romans to post soldiers at city gates to stop them
questions.correctAnswer: Persecuted them even to foreign cities
questions.explanation: Acts 26:11 (ESV): "And in raging fury against them I persecuted them even to foreign cities."

questions.question: The risen Christ told Paul his mission: to open the eyes of the Gentiles so they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God — to receive forgiveness of sins and what else?
options: A place among those who are sanctified by faith in me
The gift of the Holy Spirit as the seal of their salvation
Eternal life and a place in the heavenly kingdom
The righteousness of God through faith in Christ
questions.correctAnswer: A place among those who are sanctified by faith in me
questions.explanation: Acts 26:18 (ESV): "to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me."

questions.question: Paul stated he had not been disobedient to the heavenly vision. What did he declare to both those in Damascus, Jerusalem, Judea, and the Gentiles?
options: That they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds in keeping with their repentance
That Jesus Christ was risen from the dead as the Holy Scriptures foretold
That God had called them to salvation through faith in his Son
That the kingdom of God had come and was available to all who believed
questions.correctAnswer: That they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds in keeping with their repentance
questions.explanation: Acts 26:20 (ESV): "...that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds in keeping with their repentance."

questions.question: Festus interrupted Paul's defense with a loud voice. What did he say?
options: "Paul, you are out of your mind; your great learning is driving you out of your mind."
"Enough! The case is clear and you will be sent to Rome."
"This man speaks madness; no educated man believes in resurrection."
"You shame yourself before the king with such wild claims."
questions.correctAnswer: "Paul, you are out of your mind; your great learning is driving you out of your mind."
questions.explanation: Acts 26:24 (ESV): "And as he was saying these things in his defense, Festus said with a loud voice, 'Paul, you are out of your mind; your great learning is driving you out of your mind.'"

questions.question: Paul replied that he was not out of his mind but speaking "true and rational words." He then turned directly to Agrippa. What did he ask?
options: "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."
"King Agrippa, do you think I am lying about what I have seen?"
"King Agrippa, are you persuaded by what Moses and the prophets foretold?"
"King Agrippa, has not God shown the truth of these things to you?"
questions.correctAnswer: "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."
questions.explanation: Acts 26:27 (ESV): "King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."

questions.question: Agrippa's famous response to Paul was: "In a short time would you persuade me to be a..."?
options: Christian
believer
follower
convert
questions.explanation: Acts 26:28 (ESV): "And Agrippa said to Paul, 'In a short time would you persuade me to be a Christian?'"

questions.question: Paul replied to Agrippa saying he prayed that whether in short or long time, not only Agrippa but all his audience would become "such as I am — except for..."?
options: these chains
my imprisonment
my suffering
my bonds
questions.explanation: Acts 26:29 (ESV): "And Paul said, 'Whether short or long, I would to God that not only you but also all who hear me this day might become such as I am—except for these chains.'"

questions.question: After Paul's defense, Agrippa, Bernice, and Festus withdrew and agreed about Paul. What was their conclusion?
options: This man is doing nothing to deserve death or imprisonment
He should be sent to Caesar as quickly as possible
He is clearly innocent but we cannot contradict the Jewish leaders
He has committed no crime against Rome but may have broken Jewish law
questions.correctAnswer: This man is doing nothing to deserve death or imprisonment
questions.explanation: Acts 26:31 (ESV): "and when they had withdrawn, they said to one another, 'This man is doing nothing to deserve death or imprisonment.'"

questions.question: Agrippa said to Festus: "This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to..."?
options: Caesar
Rome
the emperor
the tribunal
questions.explanation: Acts 26:32 (ESV): "And Agrippa said to Festus, 'This man could have been set free if he had not appealed to Caesar.'"

questions.question: Paul described what Christ said he was being sent to do among the Gentiles. He was to be a "witness" to both the things Paul had seen AND what else?
options: The things in which I will appear to you
The things the prophets have written about me
The things the Holy Spirit will reveal to you
The things you will hear from the other apostles
questions.correctAnswer: The things in which I will appear to you
questions.explanation: Acts 26:16 (ESV): "...I have appeared to you for this purpose, to appoint you as a servant and witness to the things in which you have seen me and to those in which I will appear to you,"

questions.question: Paul summed up his preaching as saying nothing beyond what the prophets and Moses said would come. What two things did he say they predicted?
options: That the Christ must suffer and that, by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles
That the Christ would come as a servant and be rejected by his own people
That the Spirit would be poured out on all flesh and Gentiles would believe
That Christ would reign and Jerusalem would be exalted among the nations
questions.correctAnswer: That the Christ must suffer and that, by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles
questions.explanation: Acts 26:23 (ESV): "that the Christ must suffer and that, by being the first to rise from the dead, he would proclaim light both to our people and to the Gentiles."

questions.question: Paul told Agrippa that Jesus was the first to proclaim light to both Jews and Gentiles "by being the first to rise from the dead." What does "first to rise from the dead" mean in context?
options: The first to rise in a permanent resurrection body that death can no longer touch
The first person ever brought back to life in human history
The first Jewish resurrection prophesied in the Law of Moses
The first to rise and then remain on earth to teach the disciples
questions.correctAnswer: The first to rise in a permanent resurrection body that death can no longer touch
questions.explanation: Acts 26:23 refers to Jesus as the firstfruits of resurrection — not just a resuscitation (as with Lazarus) but the first permanent resurrection from which death is defeated.

key_verse_text: "...to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and a place among those who are sanctified by faith in me."
